preState.branchAtOrigin: 6d843f28732dd82163065cb4d2248e488f68ca0b (== main@origin; no commit of its own)
preState.workingCopy: .codegraph/ excluded by the clone's .git/info/exclude line 7; snapshot.auto-track = all(); jj status clean

findings.finding: No root .gitignore; .codegraph/.gitignore un-ignores itself, so if untracked on main it could be snapshotted into the implementer's working copy and ride into the handoff commit after `jj split` moves only the marker; the local AC4 guard read `@-`, not `@`.
findings.answer: Measured: `.codegraph/` is excluded by the clone's `.git/info/exclude` line 7 (`git check-ignore -v .codegraph/.gitignore`), `snapshot.auto-track = all()`, `jj status` clean, `jj diff --from F --to @ --name-only` empty, `.codegraph` untracked at F. Plan adds a working-copy path guard (`--to @`) to the stop condition with the rule: leave a stray path out of every commit, never rm a path you did not author, report it.

findings.finding: Scope ambiguity: the driver's message as recorded on the issue is truncated; the visible part asks for a plan handoff only, while the plan schedules every phase through the production check.
findings.answer: Plan quotes the whole message and settles the reading: the planning deliverable is the handoff alone (no code, no PR, no role started); the plan covers every later phase because the workflow runs them and the planner's charter is to plan them; the Stage 4b driver decides when each runs. Recorded as overturnable by the architect.

findings.finding: Nothing on the issue says the child produces smoke/LEGSMOKE-1138.md; it could instead be the fallback executor of the parent's smoke/LEGSMOKE-1135.md.
findings.answer: Plan settles own-key with evidence: every marker on main names the issue whose branch landed it (PRs #763-#767); the parent's AC4 requires its own PR diff to be smoke/LEGSMOKE-1135.md, so a child landing that path races the parent; the proof instructions forbid work outside this issue's smoke branch; and the previous run's identical child planned its own key (dispatch://LEGSMOKE-1131/artifact/plan-md). Flagged to the architect as overturnable.

findings.finding: AC3 has two mutually exclusive outcomes (one or two lines) and no readable fact selecting which a later phase must check.
findings.answer: Plan adds a selector: the reviewer writes `secondLineRequested: true|false` in review.json, which must agree with `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/pulls/<n>/reviews --jq '[.[] | select(.state=="CHANGES_REQUESTED")] | length'` (>=1 <=> true); expected lines = 1 + (secondLineRequested ? 1 : 0); the implementer records secondCodeHead and secondLineSha256 when true.

findings.finding: The branch pre-exists at origin, so the LEGSMOKE-1056 reset invariant (compare/B...head == ahead, B ancestor of the remote bookmark) belongs in every phase's pre-push guard; the plan's stop condition omitted it.
findings.answer: Plan adds constants B = F = 6d843f28 (no seed commit), the per-phase guard `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/compare/6d843f28...<head> --jq .status` == ahead plus the ancestor check, the 'nothing else on the branch' fact as the path set from B with .legion/LEGSMOKE-1138/ excluded (empty), and the obligation on any other answer: stop, report, re-use no recorded proof SHA.

findings.finding: The pre-state table, both sha256 values and the commit-message convention are command outputs the analyst could not re-run; no re-read step covered the hash or the convention.
findings.answer: Plan makes the hash re-derived: at implementing `printf '%s\n' "LEGSMOKE-1138: $(dispatch read --issue LEGSMOKE-1138 | sed -n 's/^Title: //p')" | sha256sum` must print 0dd91ec6...ab86 or the implementer re-derives and records expectedBytes/expectedSha256/titleAtImplementing. The convention claim now quotes the five `git log --oneline -n 5 -- smoke/` lines it rests on.

findings.finding: AC4's READY expectation asserted that a docs/solutions/ note exists, where the parent spec only permits that path.
findings.answer: Plan restates AC4 as a set relation: {marker} ⊆ S ⊆ {marker} ∪ .legion/LEGSMOKE-1138/** ∪ docs/solutions/** before retro, and {marker} ⊆ S ⊆ {marker} ∪ docs/solutions/** at READY; a docs/solutions/ note is allowed, not required by this acceptance.

findings.finding: The marker text derives from the issue title (which embeds a run-specific /tmp path) while acceptance is pinned to a byte count and hash computed at planning; nothing says which governs if the title changes.
findings.answer: Plan states the content rule as `LEGSMOKE-1138: <title as read at implementing>`; 84 / 0dd91ec6...ab86 are the expected values for the title as read on 2026-10-24; a changed title means the implementer re-derives and records both, never writes a stale line to match the planning hash.
